claims.text: The proposed alloy is based primarily on Co-Cr-Fe-Ni, with Al maintained at approximately x = 0.1 and controlled Ti additions.
Reducing Al to approximately x = 0.1 and adding Ti will significantly reduce the alloy density.
Low-density Al and Ti additions can contribute to reduced density in refractory HEAs.
The low-Al, Ti-modified alloy will maintain or enhance mechanical strength.
The low-Al, Ti-modified alloy will maintain or enhance thermal stability.
The low-Al, Ti-modified alloy will maintain or enhance irradiation resistance.
Al0.1CoCrFeNi without Ti is a single-phase alloy with strong phase stability under ion irradiation and no observed precipitates at the highest tested fluence.
Adjusting low Al and Ti levels promotes a stable, single-phase disordered microstructure.
Controlled low-Al and Ti additions minimize deleterious precipitation.
High configurational entropy reduces the thermodynamic driving force for precipitation in Al0.1CoCrFeNi.
Low atomic diffusion kinetically restricts precipitate formation in Al0.1CoCrFeNi.
Ti addition maintains high configurational entropy and lowers the thermodynamic driving force for precipitation in the proposed Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-based alloy.
Suppression of precipitation preserves mechanical integrity under extreme thermal and irradiation conditions.
Some conventional refractory HEAs containing heavy refractory elements have densities above 12 g/cm3.
Replacing Ta and W with lower-density refractory elements and adding Al and Ti has produced lower-density RHEAs with strong high-temperature performance.
Higher-Al or multiphase HEAs are more susceptible to phase separation and precipitation under irradiation.
The proposed alloy will maintain or improve stiffness and general durability relative to traditional heavy or multiphase HEAs.
The beneficial effects will diminish when Al or Ti additions exceed solubility or microstructural-stability limits.

contradictions.description: Al is characterized as a lightweight element, but lowering Al is also asserted to lower density, while higher Al content is treated as a cause of higher density. No quantitative composition or compensating Ti substitution is provided to reconcile these statements.
